newsitem.title: USA: First Union's profits shrink after charge.
newsitem.headline: First Union's profits shrink after charge.

text.p: First Union Corp. said Monday its profits slipped in the third quarter, when it took a one-time, after-tax charge of $86 million to replenish the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
The bank said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 fell 6.3 percent to $357 million, or $1.29 a share, from $381 million, or $1.36 a share.
Wall Street had expected the bank to post a profit of $1.59 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates of corporate earnings.
Without the charge for recapitalizing the Savings Association Insurance Fund, the bank would have posted earnings equal to $1.60 a share.
The Charlotte, N.C.-based bank also said it increased its provision for loan losses to $105 million from $60 million, mainly because of its credit card business.
"Our loan-loss provision has stepped up a little over the last two years and will continue," said Mal Murray, First Union's credit officer. "(Credit) card charge-offs were the overall driver."

Murray said he expected the bank's $5.4 billion credit card portfolio to show a write-off rate of between 6.0 percent and 6.5 percent this year and next. He said the write-off rate for the rest of the bank's loan businesses was 0.27 percent, which he said was "comfortable."

First Union said its operating earnings in the quarter rose to $1.60 a share from $1.36, mainly on higher income from fees. Excluding securities transactions, fee income rose 28 percent to $598 million from $466 million, it said.
For the first nine months of the year, First Union said its net income dipped to $1.04 billion, or $3.69 a share, from $1.10 billion, or $3.85 a share.
The bank said third-quarter net interest income rose 6 percent to $1.28 billion from $1.21 billion and average net loans grew to $90.5 billion from $86.0 billion.
First Union's stock gained 62.5 cents to $68.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
